Examples:
  nyx cve CVE-2021-44228 CVE-2024-3094 --json
  nyx ip 1.1.1.1 --json
  nyx recon example.com --json --timeout 30m
  nyx recon export -e example.com --json

nyx is passive-first reconnaissance for authorised engagements. Every command takes the shared
flags, and each command's own flags follow its name.

Shared flags (every command takes them; they alone may also come before the command):
  -J, --json    Print the result as one JSON object on stdout, and any error as one JSON line on stderr
  -q, --quiet   Write only warnings and errors to stderr; recon's summary is still printed
      --debug   Also write diagnostics to stderr: each failed check (recon), each request to the NVD (cve), each address probed (ip --active), and the stack of an unexpected failure

nyx cve <CVE-ID>... [flags]
  Look up CVEs in the NVD by CVE ID
  Example: nyx cve CVE-2021-44228 CVE-2024-3094 --json
cve flags:
      --fields string      Return only these fields, separated by commas, plus id; all returns every field (without it, all but affected_products and references, which are counted instead)
      --limit int          Show at most this many entries of each of affected_products and references that --fields shows
      --match string       Keep only the entries of affected_products and references that contain this text, ignoring case
      --timeout duration   Deadline for the whole call, e.g. 30s or 2m (default 60s)
      --config string      Config file (default $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/nyx/config.yaml, else ~/.config/nyx/config.yaml)
Fields accepted by --fields: id, status, published, last_modified, description, cvss_version, cvss_score, cvss_severity, cvss_vector, cvss_source, weaknesses, affected_products_count, affected_products, references_count, references, all

nyx ip <input>... [flags]
  Look up IP addresses, hostnames and CIDRs
  Example: nyx ip 1.1.1.1 --json
ip flags:
      --active             Also connect to each address that is not shared infrastructure, non-public ones included; passing it is the confirmation
      --fields string      Return only these fields, separated by commas, plus the address, hostnames, kind and failures; all returns every field the mode allows
      --timeout duration   Deadline for the whole call, e.g. 30s or 2m (default grows with the number of addresses)
Fields accepted by --fields: asn, as_name, as_prefix, rdap_netblock, rdap_org, rdap_registry, ptr, provider, provider_class, geo_country, geo_city, internetdb_ports, internetdb_hostnames, internetdb_tags, internetdb_cpes, internetdb_vulns, reverse_ip, reverse_ip_count, not_contacted, ports, tls, web (these four only with --active), all

nyx recon [domain...] [flags]
  Passive-first reconnaissance of a target's domains, organisations and netblocks
  Example: nyx recon example.com --json --timeout 30m
recon flags:
  -d, --domains-file string     File of root domains, one per line (# comments allowed)
      --org stringArray         Organisation name (repeatable)
      --asn stringArray         ASN, AS123 or 123; its announced netblocks become in scope (repeatable)
      --cidr stringArray        Netblock in CIDR notation (repeatable)
  -x, --exclude stringArray     Excluded hostname, *.wildcard or CIDR (repeatable)
      --exclude-file string     File of exclusions, one per line (# comments allowed)
  -e, --engagement string       Engagement name (default: derived from the first input)
      --passive                 Use third-party sources only; never contact target-owned systems
      --authorised              Confirm you are authorised to test this scope, for this and later runs (alias --authorized)
      --redo string             Re-perform every check of one stage (see nyx help stages)
      --skip stringArray        Stage to turn off for this run (repeatable; replaces the skip setting, and none clears it; see nyx help stages)
      --allow-large-netblocks   Proceed even if in-scope IPv4 netblocks exceed --netblock-limit
      --timeout duration        Stop by this deadline, e.g. 30m or 2h, and exit 7; run again to carry on (default: none)
      --config string           Config file (default $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/nyx/config.yaml, else ~/.config/nyx/config.yaml)
      --output-dir string       Directory in which engagement directories are created (default ".")
Stages accepted by --redo and --skip: crtsh, shodan, providerranges, resolve, wildcard, httpprobe, ports
Stages --skip refuses: resolve, wildcard, ipowner, providerranges
Tuning settings (rates, limits, ports, lists and the rest) are listed by nyx recon --help.

nyx recon export -e <engagement> [flags]
  Write everything recorded about an engagement as JSON lines
  Example: nyx recon export -e example.com --json
recon export flags:
  -e, --engagement string   Engagement name (required)
      --output string       Write to this file, replacing it atomically, instead of stdout
      --current             Export only records that are current
      --kind stringArray    Export only this kind (repeatable); the kinds are listed below
      --output-dir string   Directory in which engagement directories are created (default ".")
      --config string       Config file (default $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/nyx/config.yaml, else ~/.config/nyx/config.yaml)
Kinds accepted by --kind: asn, candidate_rank, code_mention, dns_claim, email_posture, excluded, finding, historical_address, hostname, http_port, ip, ip_hostname, ip_owner, netblock, open_port, organisation, origin_check, port_check, provider_range, registration, reported_port, resolution, root, script, script_parsed, sensitive_hit, server_address, shodan_netblock, storage, storage_account, storage_object, storage_ref, takeover_http, third_party, unresolved, url, web_identifier, web_posture, web_service, wildcard, input, exclusion

Help:
  nyx help findings    Finding types and their default severities
  nyx help [command]   The help of nyx, or of one command or topic: the same as --help
  nyx help stages      The stages, in run order, and what each one contacts and does

Flags:
      --version   Print the version and exit
  -h, --help      Help for nyx

Exit codes: 0 success, 1 system error, 2 usage error, 3 not found, 7 partial result, 130/143/129 interrupted (SIGINT/SIGTERM/SIGHUP)
